answer: In PoA, trust propagates by bounded-length random walks over an attestation graph, so each vertex receives weight from the walk distribution launched at trusted seeds. An unrooted sybil cluster is a hollow reef: its identities share a sparse external cut, giving low conductance and little probability of entry or escape. Min-cut transitivity bounds then limit its reachable mass—and hence aggregate voting weight—to a function of boundary volume, not its inflated membership.
